findings.text: The opening tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, all before the study begins. This part works well.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: Someone who comes to the Athena site expects a page about Athena, but the title and almost all of the content are about a different project, firstmate. Only the second lede paragraph explains that the page is a demonstration, so a reader who skims the title may think they are on the wrong page.

The next step is easy to find. It links from the top to a section that gives prerequisites ("git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl..."), the clone command, `./setup.sh` and a first command to try, `athena ask "add a changelog"`.
findings.source: Header lede: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the section "Next steps"

findings.text: This link is aimed at the repository owner, not a visitor. Placed next to the newcomer's next step, it suggests the reader has decisions waiting and could send them somewhere they don't need to go.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: "Start here" uses terms that its own "Words used first" list does not define: place, exit 75, spawn, ship and captain call. A newcomer has to jump to the Glossary to follow what is meant to be the gentle introduction.
findings.source: "One piece of work, start to finish": "the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued" and "A PR-based ship's place is freed once its ready PR is recorded"

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine breakdown of firstmate, with exit codes, guards and lock behaviour. It shows the claim-to-source tracing the lede promises, but it is far more detail than a newcomer needs to judge Athena, and the page never points out which part a skimmer can stop at.
findings.source: Sections "Transitions" (cards t1 to t12) and "Claims and sources" (c1 to c45)

findings.text: The page tells the reader how to check its central promise themselves. Each claim links to exact file lines at the pinned commit, which makes the claim of traceability concrete.
findings.source: "Next steps": "Check a statement: follow a bracketed claim id to the claim, then its source link to the file and lines in firstmate at the pinned commit."

findings.text: This section and the footer describe internal repository layout, which means nothing to a first-time visitor. Neither says where that folder lives.
findings.source: "About this page": "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
